purpose: Audit current mechanistic/generalization output against independent aggregate evidence, with special attention to high-capacity contradictions. Validation-only analogues remain held out and never become predictors or training targets.

hard_exact_boundary_contradictions.mapped_boundary: Entire Rapa Nui island; exact EU5 location_tag=rapa_nui
hard_exact_boundary_contradictions.local_food_and_pressure: low-trade isolated island; traditional sweet-potato dryland agriculture, rock gardens/mulch and marine foods; island-wide land, freshwater, nutrient and drought constraints
shock_and_semantic_caveats: rock-garden extent and nitrogen-fixation regime are disputed/sensitivity drivers
post-contact decline is not used as a target
citation_details: Puleston et al., Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution 5 (2017), abstract and Table 2: 3,134 ha suitable for traditional dryland sweet potato; low-N average approximately 3,500 and high-N approximately 17,500 sustainable people, with higher values possible under selected assumptions.

Puleston et al. (2017), Results/Discussion: modeled yields are highly sensitive to nitrogen inputs, fallow/continuous cultivation and social assumptions; the interval is retained as a validation envelope rather than a 1337 training label.
hard_exact_boundary_contradictions.interpretation: This is a real model contradiction, not a boundary artifact. The current output is above the cited high endpoint by 1.96x. The result blocks a claim of globally generalized capacity until island area, crop nitrogen/fallow treatment, marine-food caps and uncertainty propagation are audited. It does not authorize a Rapa Nui-specific multiplier or a global downscale.

soft_or_unresolved_high_capacity_contrad.reason: One EU5 location is a broad proxy for an archaeological settlement system; the published interval is not a complete province-scale boundary.
The archaeological/city hinterland envelope is not equivalent to the broad EU5 selector; city provisioning and oasis trade are unresolved.
The mapped EU5 footprint and Classic Maya settlement/forest-management boundary are not yet equivalent; the interval is not a same-boundary 1337 target.

gate_effect.reason: An exact-boundary independent food-limit interval fails by 3.42x. The failure must be explained through shared physical features, land allocation, nutrient/fallow assumptions, marine-food caps and uncertainty—not hidden by a regional multiplier or excluded from the report.

required_followup: Recompute the Rapa Nui island case with the same area, soil/nutrient, fallow/rotation, marine-food and uncertainty conventions used by the global model; preserve the published low/high nitrogen scenarios as an external holdout.

Run leave-one-source-family and leave-one-island-out generalization with Rapa Nui held out; report whether any challenger reduces the 3.42x contradiction without worsening Iceland/England interval coverage.
Keep Engaruka, Palmyra and Petén as boundary-repair queues; their large ratios are not admissible evidence until the archaeological/hinterland polygons are closed.
Do not alter global normalization or introduce island/region correction factors while this gate is failing.
